note: Both sets cover the same eight facts — window azimuth 0, 50° solar altitude at fall equinox noon, the louver spacing algorithm and its simplified Height = D*1.2, the 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, the tapered truncated isosceles triangle louver profile, the 25° longitudinal structural bend, and the powder-coated finish. A states every value in full and correctly bound, whereas B truncates the bend condition ('along the louver longit') and records the simplified formula as the bare fragment 'D*1.2' while pushing the general formula into its conditions field. Both repeat facts under two names (four pairs in A, three in B), so A's only real drawback is slightly greater redundancy.
remarks: Both sets miss the stated design fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths (after the taper), and neither captures the 25° bend's function of directing reflected light onto the ceiling/adjacent louvers and reducing direct glare, nor the screen transparency noted alongside the powder-coated finish. A states the powder-coated finish twice under two names ('louver' and 'Harvest Shade Screen'); the text attributes it to the screen, so the louver binding is a mild relabeling rather than a separate fact. B's claim 1 is a near-duplicate of its claim 9 with the formula split awkwardly between value and conditions.
